scope: 25 exact historical keys outside other assignments; operators and full endpoint scopes inspected against the already inspected source treatments. No final-value approval inferred.

rows.review_disposition: 612D/069F must retain Quiberon as a major military setback and demonstration of coordination failure within a multi-causal defeat. Do not make this one episode the end of all royalism or the sole cause of armed defeat.

29CD can internalize preparation through official lists, rival assemblies and reserved verification. Preserve the distinction between manipulation before voting and the subsequent Floréal purge of 127 elected deputies.

667E can internalize the law preserving 500 Convention members and institutional habits. Retain its unpopularity and the failure of Vendémiaire enabling its operation, rather than representing continuity as consensual.

7EDE/2E013 must retain Fructidor hardening negotiation terms, inducing Austria to stop delaying while breaking the British talks. Chronological follows may retire with these contrasting consequences explicit.

381386 can internalize the first categorical anti-noble citizenship law and its weak implementation. Retire the unbound revolutionary-citizenship label without dropping either legal discrimination or enforcement limits.

C455/B438 can retain the regional connection between Catholic royalism and schism. B973 must preserve early southern sectarian conflict preceding the oath; it cannot stand for a universal oath-caused origin of all Midi royalism.

60C460 must retain local autonomy, attempted metropolitan control, the restoration of slavery and renewed resistance in the contingent path to independence. Keep British and French interventions and losses distinct.
C4FA/C479 can internalize British intervention within great-power policy, preserving material support and strategic self-interest rather than implying unconditional restorationist commitment.

C83/9DE8 must retain the coexistence of widespread abstention and a clear anti-Convention result among participating assemblies. Neither universal restorationist mandate nor politically meaningless voting is supported.

CB77/667E must distinguish the large formal vote for the constitution from the unpopular, confused and manipulated continuity vote. Retiring the vague relationship is conditional on retaining this contrast.

4E189 can internalize hunger protest and nostalgic invocations of Robespierre as evidence of grievance. Preserve attribution; the testimony is not proof that his government had protected all poor people.

21A/48B must retain Hoche’s movement into the constitutionally protected Paris zone and Barras’s encouragement as preparation for the coup. Do not reduce this to a neutral chronological troop movement.

C83/9DE8 can internalize abstention as one phase of disengagement. Keep the 1797 result distinct from limited later resistance to coups; page 329 alone does not support every later phase or popular approval.

DA4B/0D88 must preserve domestic advantage from Bonaparte’s absence as a motive for approving Egypt. Success and failure could both benefit the Directors; this does not mean they expected only failure or that domestic calculation was the whole strategy.

F4D/B319/CB77 must preserve fiscal reconstruction alienating the propertied constituency the regime claimed to represent. The practical political contradiction does not logically refute every property-qualification argument.

47D/F4D/3F2B must retain the first five Directors’ republican reliability, limited demonstrated collective ability and initial balancing line. Do not attribute every later policy phase to the unchanged original personnel or solely to page 321.

7EDE can internalize Campo Formio leaving imperial compensation and the Rhine settlement open because Austrian recognition could not bind the Empire. Retain Rastadt and the postponed territorial costs.

DA4B must preserve Egypt as an alternative to direct invasion of Britain, with speculative India/wealth logic and naval and port constraints. Unlike the erroneous Nile alternative elsewhere, this alternative relationship is supported.

33CF/1DB can retain the June 1789 maximum-concession programme as a later restorationist baseline. Do not identify all subsequent manifestos with the original session; preserve the source’s 303 date discrepancy against 297/310.

48B/F4D/29CD must preserve Fructidor arrests, press closures and annulments as a phase of electoral authoritarianism. Floréal is a later distinct intervention, not the event that enacted all Fructidor measures.
48B/F4D/29CD must retain Fructidor as the transition to a more coercive Second Directory. This is a regime phase change, not creation of all Directory institutions or identity with later Floréal.

1DB/33CF can retain the Royal Session programme as the later maximum-concession baseline. The relationship is a substantive back-reference, not proof that all royalists shared identical later programmes.

21A/F4D must retain dependence on the army making military disillusionment dangerous to survival. Page 340 is a prospective closing argument, not evidence that Brumaire had already occurred or was inevitable.

3F2B can internalize the Directory’s permission and subsequent containment of constitutional circles. Preserve the mixed anti-royalist coalition and closure when democratic language or electoral reform demands exceeded official purposes.

5193/F6ED must retain demonetization and immediate deflation on 324. Later fiscal reconstruction on 333–334 requires FF3E/B319 and intervening measures; retire an automatic successful-reconstruction causal claim.
